title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Validation and Cutover Verification
verification_method: Focused S9P6P2-0008/0009/0010 requirement-home tests, full Release no-build solution tests, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, Release build, SpecTrace JSON validation, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers the current single-active-path runtime behavior for preferred-address validation before migration, matching PATH_RESPONSE emission on the preferred-address candidate path, and exclusive non-probing sends after validated IPv4 or IPv6 preferred-address cutover.
expected_result: The chosen preferred address remains a candidate path and does not promote before validation, a protected PATH_CHALLENGE on that candidate path receives a matching PATH_RESPONSE on the same path, and once validation completes later non-probing sends are emitted only on the chosen preferred-address path.
procedure: Run the focused S9P6P2-0008/0009/0010 requirement-home filter.
Run the full Release no-build solution test suite.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The runtime has an active original path before preferred-address traffic arrives.
Peer transport parameters carry a preferred_address with IPv4, IPv6, connection ID, and stateless reset token values.
The PATH_CHALLENGE proof has 1-RTT open packet protection material installed.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim complete preferred-address closure for S9P6P2, multipath behavior, public migration APIs, or hosted interop success.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-04. The focused S9P6P2-0008/0009/0010 filter passed 5/5, Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the full Release no-build solution suite passed 4088/4088, core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 379 artifacts, and generated triage resolves the targeted requirements as trace-clean.
